days.title: Get to know your guitar
days.description: Hold the guitar in playing position. Identify the headstock, tuning pegs, neck, frets, strings, soundhole, and bridge. Pluck each open string to hear its sound.
days.tip: Sit upright with good posture; a classical guitar position can reduce strain

days.title: Tune your guitar
days.description: Download a free tuner app (or use a clip-on tuner). Tune each string (E-A-D-G-B-e) until it's perfectly in pitch.
days.tip: Tune from flat to sharp to avoid over-tightening and breaking strings

days.title: Master the 'E' chord shape
days.description: Place your fingers for an open E major chord. Strum slowly, checking each string for a clear, ringing sound. Adjust finger pressure as needed.
days.tip: Press down with the very tips of your fingers, not the pads, to avoid muting adjacent strings

days.title: The 'A' chord challenge
days.description: Learn the open A major chord shape. Practice switching between E major and A major 10 times, aiming for smooth transitions.
days.tip: Try to move all fingers simultaneously when changing chords, rather than one by one

days.title: Strumming basics
days.description: With your E major chord held, practice a simple down-up strumming pattern (e.g., down-down-up-up-down-up). Keep a consistent rhythm.
days.tip: Use your wrist, not your whole arm, for a more relaxed and fluid strumming motion

days.title: Your first song: 'Horse With No Name'
days.description: Learn the two-chord progression (Em and D) for 'A Horse With No Name'. Practice strumming and switching between these chords.
days.tip: Focus on the rhythm of the chord changes first, then worry about perfect sound

days.title: Week 1 check-in and goals
days.description: Play through the chords and song you've learned. Identify what felt good and what areas need more practice. Set a small goal for next week.
days.tip: Record yourself playing to objectively hear your progress and identify areas for improvement
